section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Papillon Journey is a JRPG-like, game-based online training platform in system and software engineering, where players advance their education and develop their engineering skills through quests, challenges, mini-games, and immersive storylines.
This document presents our vision for the project: what it is, why it matters, and how we plan to make it succeed.

section.title: Purpose
section.simpara: Formal and model-driven approaches to software development emerged in the 1960s–1980s through close collaboration between academia and industries operating under extreme safety and reliability demands — the earliest being defence, aerospace, nuclear power, and railway signalling. Their use broadened during the 1990s–2000s to other life-critical (automotive, medical devices) and high-stakes areas (finance, hardware design). They are now gradually entering mainstream software engineering, finding applications in cloud infrastructure, telecommunications, blockchain, and cybersecurity.
Papillon Journey aims to build on this momentum by tackling three major hindrances to wider adoption:

listitem.simpara: Limited exposure: the historical confinement of these approaches to high-assurance projects has unintentionally reinforced the misconception that they are irrelevant to the daily concerns of most software professionals. Demonstrating their effectiveness through large-scale open-source initiatives in web, mobile, and game development will help dispel this view.

Fragmented tooling: companies favour tools that integrate seamlessly into existing workflows, but those supporting formal methods — narrowly specialised and rarely interoperable — often fail to do so. Chrysal Studio, the research subproject of Papillon Journey, will explore and prototype a unified integrated engineering environment to change that.

Inverted pedagogy: children learn to add and multiply long before they ever hear of ring theory — and only if they choose to. Yet formal modelling is typically taught the other way around: heavy on theory, light on practice, and illustrated with simplistic ‘toy examples’ that bear little resemblance to the challenges encountered in industry.

section.simpara: Papillon Journey is a cross-platform game, playable directly in a web browser or through native applications for Windows desktops and iPads. It is also libre: its source code, models, and documentation are intentionally designed to teach formal engineering by example. Anyone may study it, contribute to it, and adapt it to their own needs, as long as derivative works remain libre. All of this aims to raise the visibility of formal modelling techniques by providing a transparent, participatory, and engaging real-world use case accessible across various devices.

At first, the game development will rely on the current patchwork of disjointed formal methods tools. But as Chrysal Studio matures, it will progressively take their place, until it can fully support the engineering of both itself and Papillon Journey.

Fusing the experience of a JRPG (for example, Final Fantasy) with that of a training platform (such as Coursera) without breaking immersion is no small task. One thing is certain, though: learners will spend most of their time practising. The very nature of JRPGs will steer Papillon Journey away from the pitfall of inverted pedagogy.
